calls.reason: This is an open-ended claim about what AGI requires, with no deadline. ARC Prize's Astra results show progress but don't declare AGI, and the AGI Society says Astra's AGI status isn't supported. Nothing shows that the alternative approaches are or aren't needed.

Lake and Baroni only tentatively link weak systematicity to data hunger. The NYT reporting ties data hunger to corner-cutting but also cites competition and speed. Nothing connects the whole chain from weak generalization to developers' choices.

The cited studies cover a tiny decoder and repeated-data setups, and a 2026 study finds that sparsity delays saturation. That is too narrow to settle a broad open-ended forecast stated as an expectation.

Epoch projects public text running out between 2026 and 2032, but that is a projection. Musk's 'exhausted' remark has no measurement behind it, and synthetic-data studies blur the supply limit. No actual crossing is documented.

'Never' and 'always' can't be settled by a limited set of studies. OMEGA shows continuing failures, while the length-generalization and reasoning-representation papers show improvement. Neither side is shown for good.

Two peer-reviewed 2023 NeurIPS studies (Mystery Blocksworld and Faith and Fate) show reasoning and planning collapsing on unfamiliar variants and out-of-distribution cases in standard LLMs. Only specially trained meta-learning models (MLC) do better.
